title: prefill+decode: integrate chunked/speculative prefill with kernel scheduler and stage-overlap optimizations
author: Asha Patel
body:
Motivation: Reduce end-to-end per-request latency and increase GPU utilization by combining chunked prefill, speculative prefill, and stage-overlap execution with the runtime kernel scheduler and improved KV-cache semantics. Previous work iterated on each optimization in isolation; this PR integrates them and resolves contention between speculative prefill retries and the kernel scheduler's co-scheduling heuristics.

Summary of changes:
- Integrate chunked prefill path into kernel scheduler: prefill chunks are now exposed as schedulable units so the scheduler can colocate decode work and prefill chunks across GPUs to improve pipeline overlap.
- Speculative prefill improvements: introduce a lightweight speculative token generator that runs on a lower-priority stream and uses a bounded lookahead window to warm KV caches without stalling primary streams. Added backpressure signals to avoid overload.
- Stage-overlap orchestration: enhanced cross-stage signaling to allow decode to begin on already-prefilled KV slices while remaining prefill chunks complete; avoids full prefill barrier for many workloads.
- KV cache changes: moved to per-chunk cache entries with eviction-aware reference counting so speculative warmups do not evict primary cache entries. Also added metrics for speculative hit-rate.
- Kernel scheduler tuning: new heuristics to prioritize low-latency request tails and to co-schedule small prefill chunks with pending decode kernels for the same session.
- Continuous batching tweaks: adjusted batching window for mixed prefill/decode workloads to reduce tail latency while keeping throughput high.
- Tests & benchmarks: end-to-end microbench harness updates and unit tests for the scheduler, kv-cache reference counting, and speculative path.

Benchmarks (internal microbench on 8xA100; p50/p95 latency measured for short-chat workload, smaller-batch production config):
- Baseline (before): p50=72ms, p95=240ms, throughput=120 req/s
- After (this PR): p50=56ms (-22%), p95=185ms (-23%), throughput=162 req/s (+35%)
- Speculative warmup median KV hit-rate: 78% for 8-token lookahead (measured on mixed traffic traces).

Implementation notes:
- Introduced SchedulerChunk abstraction (runtime/scheduler/chunk.h, .cc) that allows the existing kernel scheduler to reason about chunked prefill units.
- Speculative prefill path lives in runtime/prefill/speculative_prefill.* and hooks into the request router with low-priority QoS.
- KV cache moved from a single session-key map to a per-chunk namespace (runtime/kv_cache/chunked_cache.*). Reference counts tracked per entry to avoid premature eviction by speculative runs.
- Added feature flag redwood.runtime.prefill_speculative_enabled to gate rollout and allow canary testing.

Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests for scheduler chunk admission and eviction semantics
- [x] Integration tests for prefill/decode overlap
- [x] Bench harness updates and results attached
- [x] Feature flag + docs note for rollout

- runtime/scheduler/chunk.cc
- runtime/prefill/speculative_prefill.cc

runtime/prefill/speculative_prefill.cc: +// run speculative generator on low-priority stream; bounded lookahead = 8 tokens
runtime/kv_cache/chunked_cache.cc: +// use atomic refcount per entry to avoid eviction during speculative warmups
review_comments: Diego Ramos: The SchedulerChunk abstraction looks good; please add a comment explaining lifecycle guarantees for chunks that span multiple GPUs.
Asha Patel: Added explanation in chunk.h and expanded tests to cover multi-gpu lifecycle (see test_chunk_admission.cc).
Marta Liu: Bench numbers look promising — can you run the end-to-end canary on dedicated-small and post results? Also add a toggle to disable speculative prefill per-customer.
Asha Patel: Ran canary on dedicated-small and attached results in bench/micro/bench_prefill_decode.py output. Added customer-scoped toggle (feature flag accepts customer_id override).
Samir Khanna: I saw a CI flake on scheduler tests on first run; guessed deadlock in admission path. Can you double-check locking?
Asha Patel: Found a lock inversion in scheduler.cc; fixed by using admission mutex ordering and added deterministic test to reproduce. CI re-ran and passed.
merge_info: Merged by Diego Ramos via squash on 2026-02-26. Merge commit message summarized bench numbers and feature flag enablement.
release_notes: Performance: integrated chunked + speculative prefill with kernel scheduler and stage-overlap to reduce latency and increase throughput. Feature gated under redwood.runtime.prefill_speculative_enabled. See docs/notes/prefill_speculative.md for rollout instructions.
notes_for_release: Canary rollout recommended: enable feature flag for 5% of dedicated-small capacity, monitor speculative-kv-hit-rate and scheduler contention metrics. Disable per-customer via feature flag if issues observed.
author_notes: This PR stitches together several performance optimizations previously landed independently. The feature flag allows rolling back the speculative warmup independently of scheduler heuristics. Follow-up work: refine co-scheduling heuristics for very large models and add dynamic chunk size selection based on recent seq-length distribution.
